    ∀ l : List α, (insertBy le x l).Perm (x :: l)
  | [] => List.Perm.refl _

    unfold insertBy
    split
    · exact List.Perm.refl _
    · exact ((perm_insertBy le x ys).cons y).trans (List.Perm.swap x y ys)

    ∀ l : List α, (isort le l).Perm l

      (insertBy le x l).Pairwise (fun a b => le a b = true)

  | y :: ys, h => by
    rw [List.pairwise_cons] at h
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
    unfold insertBy
    split
    next hxy =>
      rw [List.pairwise_cons]
      refine ⟨fun z hz => ?_, List.pairwise_cons.2 ⟨h1, h2⟩⟩
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hz with hzy | hz
      · rw [hzy]; exact hxy
      · exact trans _ _ _ hxy (h1 z hz)

      rw [List.pairwise_cons]
      refine ⟨fun z hz => ?_, pairwise_insertBy le trans total x ys h2⟩
      have hz' := (perm_insertBy le x ys).mem_iff.1 hz
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hz' with hzx | hz'
      · rw [hzx]

        · exact absurd h hxy

/-- Center a single string within a field of `width` characters, padding with spaces.
If the string is already at least `width` long, it is returned unchanged.
Otherwise the total padding `width - len` is split into a left part `pad / 2`
and a right part `pad - pad / 2` (so the right side gets the extra space when odd). -/
def centerStr (s : String) (width : Nat) : String :=
  if width ≤ s.length then s
  else "".pushn ' ' ((width - s.length) / 2) ++ s ++
       "".pushn ' ' ((width - s.length) - (width - s.length) / 2)

def center {n : Nat} (input : Vector String n) (width : Nat) : Vector String n :=
  input.map (fun s => centerStr s width)

theorem center_long {n : Nat} (input : Vector String n) (width : Nat) (i : Nat) (h : i < n)
    (hw : width ≤ input[i].length) :
    (center input width)[i] = input[i] := by
  simp only [center, Vector.getElem_map]
  unfold centerStr
  rw [if_pos hw]

sum (together with the original length) to `width`, and which are balanced:
the right padding equals the left padding or exceeds it by exactly one. -/
theorem center_short {n : Nat} (input : Vector String n) (width : Nat) (i : Nat) (h : i < n)
    (hw : input[i].length < width) :
    ∃ l r : Nat,
      (center input width)[i] = "".pushn ' ' l ++ input[i] ++ "".pushn ' ' r ∧
      l + input[i].length + r = width ∧
      l ≤ r ∧ r ≤ l + 1 := by
  refine ⟨(width - input[i].length) / 2,
          (width - input[i].length) - (width - input[i].length) / 2, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [center, Vector.getElem_map]
    unfold centerStr
    rw [if_neg (Nat.not_le.mpr hw)]
  · omega
  · omega
  · omega

  simp only [center, Vector.getElem_map]

/-- Clip a single float into the range `[lo, hi]`.
    If `x < lo` the result is `lo`; otherwise if `x > hi` the result is `hi`;
    otherwise the result is `x` itself. -/
def clipScalar (x lo hi : Float) : Float :=
  if x < lo then lo else if x > hi then hi else x

def clip {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (min max : Float) : Vector Float n :=
  a.map (fun x => clipScalar x min max)

/-- Pointwise characterization: every entry of the clipped vector is
    the clipped version of the corresponding entry. -/
theorem clip_getElem {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (lo hi : Float)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (clip a lo hi)[i] = clipScalar a[i] lo hi := by
  simp [clip]

/-- Explicit pointwise formula. -/
theorem clip_getElem_eq {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (lo hi : Float)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (clip a lo hi)[i] =
      (if a[i] < lo then lo else if a[i] > hi then hi else a[i]) := by
  rw [clip_getElem]
  rfl

/-- Entries below the lower bound are replaced by the lower bound. -/
theorem clip_below {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (lo hi : Float)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < n) (hlt : a[i] < lo) :
    (clip a lo hi)[i] = lo := by
  rw [clip_getElem_eq, if_pos hlt]

/-- Entries (not below the lower bound but) above the upper bound are
    replaced by the upper bound. -/
theorem clip_above {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (lo hi : Float)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < n) (hnlt : ¬ a[i] < lo) (hgt : a[i] > hi) :
    (clip a lo hi)[i] = hi := by
  rw [clip_getElem_eq, if_neg hnlt, if_pos hgt]

/-- Entries within the range are left unchanged. -/
theorem clip_within {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (lo hi : Float)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < n) (hnlt : ¬ a[i] < lo) (hngt : ¬ a[i] > hi) :
    (clip a lo hi)[i] = a[i] := by
  rw [clip_getElem_eq, if_neg hnlt, if_neg hngt]

    original entry. -/
theorem clip_cases {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (lo hi : Float)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (clip a lo hi)[i] = lo ∨ (clip a lo hi)[i] = hi ∨ (clip a lo hi)[i] = a[i] := by
  by_cases h1 : a[i] < lo
  · exact Or.inl (clip_below a lo hi i h h1)
  · by_cases h2 : a[i] > hi
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inl (clip_above a lo hi i h h1 h2))
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inr (clip_within a lo hi i h h1 h2))

  (List.range (n + 1)).foldl
    (fun acc i => acc + arr1.getD i 0 * arr2.getD (n - i) 0) 0

  if arr1.isEmpty || arr2.isEmpty then []
  else (List.range (arr1.length + arr2.length - 1)).map (convolutionSum arr1 arr2)

theorem convolve_nil_left (b : List Float) : convolve [] b = [] := by
  simp [convolve]

/-- Convolution with an empty right list is empty. -/
theorem convolve_nil_right (a : List Float) : convolve a [] = [] := by
  simp [convolve]

/-- Count of the elements of a list of floats that are not equal to `0.0`
    (with respect to `==` on `Float`). -/
def countNZ : List Float → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | x :: xs => (if x == 0.0 then 0 else 1) + countNZ xs

/-- Number of nonzero entries of a vector of floats. -/
def nonzero {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Float n) : Nat :=
  countNZ arr.toArray.toList

/-! ## Specification -/

/-- Characterization: `countNZ` is the length of the list filtered to nonzero elements. -/
theorem countNZ_eq_filter (l : List Float) :
    countNZ l = (l.filter (fun x => !(x == 0.0))).length := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    cases h : x == 0.0 <;> simp [countNZ, List.filter_cons, h, ih] <;> omega

/-- `nonzero` equals the number of entries that are not `== 0.0`. -/
theorem nonzero_spec {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Float n) :
    nonzero arr = (arr.toArray.toList.filter (fun x => !(x == 0.0))).length := by
  unfold nonzero
  exact countNZ_eq_filter _

/-- Counting is additive over concatenation. -/
theorem countNZ_append (l1 l2 : List Float) :
    countNZ (l1 ++ l2) = countNZ l1 + countNZ l2 := by
  induction l1 with
  | nil => simp [countNZ]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [List.cons_append, countNZ, ih]
    omega

/-- The count never exceeds the list length. -/
theorem countNZ_le (l : List Float) : countNZ l ≤ l.length := by
  induction l with
  | nil => exact Nat.le_refl 0
  | cons x xs ih =>
    cases h : x == 0.0 <;> simp [countNZ, h] <;> omega

/-- The number of nonzero entries is at most the vector length. -/
theorem nonzero_le {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Float n) : nonzero arr ≤ n := by
  have h := countNZ_le arr.toArray.toList
  have hs : arr.toArray.toList.length = n := arr.size_toArray
  unfold nonzero
  omega

/-- If every element is nonzero, the count is the full length. -/
theorem countNZ_all_nonzero (l : List Float)
    (h : ∀ x ∈ l, (x == 0.0) = false) : countNZ l = l.length := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    have hx : (x == 0.0) = false := h x (by simp)
    have hr := ih (fun y hy => h y (by simp [hy]))
    simp [countNZ, hx, hr] <;> omega

    (h : ∀ x ∈ l, (x == 0.0) = true) : countNZ l = 0 := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    have hx : (x == 0.0) = true := h x (by simp)
    have hr := ih (fun y hy => h y (by simp [hy]))
    simp [countNZ, hx, hr]

    (h : ∀ x ∈ arr.toArray.toList, (x == 0.0) = false) : nonzero arr = n := by
  have hs : arr.toArray.toList.length = n := arr.size_toArray
  unfold nonzero
  rw [countNZ_all_nonzero _ h, hs]

/-- `prodUpTo a k` is the product of the first `k` entries of `a`
(entries at indices `≥ n` are treated as `1`). -/
def prodUpTo {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) : Nat → Int
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => prodUpTo a k * (if h : k < n then a[k]'h else 1)

/-- Cumulative (prefix) product: entry `i` is `a[0] * a[1] * ... * a[i]`. -/
def cumProd {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) : Vector Int n :=
  Vector.ofFn fun i => prodUpTo a (i.val + 1)

/-- Specification: the first entry of the cumulative product is the first entry of `a`. -/

    (cumProd a)[0] = a[0] := by
  simp only [cumProd, Vector.getElem_ofFn]
  show prodUpTo a 0 * (if h : 0 < n then a[0]'h else 1) = a[0]
  rw [dif_pos h]
  exact Int.one_mul _

the current entry of `a`. Together with `cumProd_zero` this determines `cumProd`
uniquely. -/

    (cumProd a)[i + 1] = (cumProd a)[i] * a[i + 1] := by
  simp only [cumProd, Vector.getElem_ofFn]
  show prodUpTo a (i + 1) * (if h : i + 1 < n then a[i + 1]'h else 1)
      = prodUpTo a (i + 1) * a[i + 1]
  rw [dif_pos h]

  Vector.ofFn fun i => pre a (i.val + 1)

  getElem mat ij h := mat ⟨ij.1, h.1⟩ ⟨ij.2, h.2⟩

`arr[i][i+k]`; for `k ≤ 0` the i-th entry is `arr[i+|k|][i]`, where entries
that fall outside the matrix (possible due to the declared length) are `0`. -/
def diagonal {n : Nat} (arr : Matrix n n Int) (k : Int) : Vector Int (if k > 0 then n - k.natAbs else n + k.natAbs) :=
  Vector.ofFn fun i =>
    if k > 0 then
      (if h : i.val + k.natAbs < n ∧ i.val < n then arr ⟨i.val, h.2⟩ ⟨i.val + k.natAbs, h.1⟩ else 0)
    else
      (if h : i.val + k.natAbs < n ∧ i.val < n then arr ⟨i.val + k.natAbs, h.1⟩ ⟨i.val, h.2⟩ else 0)

      = arr ⟨i, by omega⟩ ⟨i + k.natAbs, hi⟩ := by
  have h2 : i < n := by omega
  simp [diagonal, hk, hi, h2]

    (i : Nat) (hi : i + k.natAbs < n) :

      = arr ⟨i + k.natAbs, hi⟩ ⟨i, by omega⟩ := by
  have h2 : i < n := by omega
  have hk' : ¬ (0 < k) := Int.not_lt.mpr hk
  simp [diagonal, hk', hi, h2]

  have hn : ¬ (i + k.natAbs < n) := Nat.not_lt.mpr hi
  simp [diagonal, hk', hn]

  Vector.ofFn fun k => mat ⟨k.val / n, flatten2_div_lt k⟩ ⟨k.val % n, flatten2_mod_lt k⟩

theorem flatten2_index_lt {m n : Nat} (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n) :
    i.val * n + j.val < m * n := by
  have h1 : (i.val + 1) * n ≤ m * n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right n i.2
  rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at h1
  have := j.2

  · exact ⟨(k : Int), by rw [ha, hk, Int.natCast_mul]⟩
  · exact ⟨-(k : Int), by rw [ha, hk, Int.natCast_mul, Int.mul_neg]⟩

  · exact ⟨(m : Int), by rw [hm, Int.natCast_mul, ← hd]⟩
  · have h2 : -d = (d.natAbs : Int) := by

/-- Membership of a value `x` in bin `j`: `bins[j] ≤ x < bins[j+1]`. -/
def inBin {m : Nat} (bins : Vector Float m) (j : Fin (m - 1)) (x : Float) : Bool :=
  have h := j.isLt
  decide (bins[j.val]'(by omega) ≤ x) && decide (x < bins[j.val + 1]'(by omega))

/-- Add one data point to the histogram (incrementing every bin it belongs to). -/
def addPoint {m : Nat} (bins : Vector Float m) (hist : Vector Int (m - 1)) (x : Float) :
    Vector Int (m - 1) :=
  Vector.ofFn (fun j => hist[j.val] + (if inBin bins j x then 1 else 0))

def histogram_helper {n m : Nat} (data : Vector Float n) (bins : Vector Float m)
    (hist : Vector Int (m - 1)) (index : Int) : Vector Int (m - 1) :=
  if index < 0 then hist
  else (data.toList.drop index.toNat).foldl (addPoint bins) hist

def histogram {n m : Nat} (data : Vector Float n) (bins : Vector Float m) : Vector Int (m - 1) :=
  histogram_helper data bins (Vector.replicate (m - 1) 0) 0

theorem foldl_addPoint_get {m : Nat} (bins : Vector Float m) (j : Nat) (hj : j < m - 1) :
    ∀ (l : List Float) (hist : Vector Int (m - 1)),
      (l.foldl (addPoint bins) hist)[j] = hist[j] + (l.countP (inBin bins ⟨j, hj⟩) : Int)
  | [], hist => by simp
  | x :: l, hist => by
      rw [List.foldl_cons, foldl_addPoint_get bins j hj l, List.countP_cons]
      simp only [addPoint, Vector.getElem_ofFn]
      by_cases h : inBin bins ⟨j, hj⟩ x = true <;> simp [h] <;> omega

/-- Specification: bin `j` of the histogram counts the data points lying in bin `j`. -/
theorem histogram_spec {n m : Nat} (data : Vector Float n) (bins : Vector Float m)
    (j : Nat) (hj : j < m - 1) :
    (histogram data bins)[j] = (data.toList.countP (inBin bins ⟨j, hj⟩) : Int) := by
  have h : histogram data bins
      = data.toList.foldl (addPoint bins) (Vector.replicate (m - 1) 0) := by
    simp [histogram, histogram_helper]
  rw [h, foldl_addPoint_get bins j hj]
  simp

/-- Helper with a negative index leaves the histogram untouched. -/
theorem histogram_helper_neg {n m : Nat} (data : Vector Float n) (bins : Vector Float m)
    (hist : Vector Int (m - 1)) (index : Int) (h : index < 0) :
    histogram_helper data bins hist index = hist := by
  simp [histogram_helper, h]

  simp only [histogram_helper, h, if_false]
  exact foldl_addPoint_get bins j hj _ hist

/-- Pointwise (fuzzy) intersection of two vectors of floats:
    the result is truncated to the shorter length, and each entry is the
    minimum of the corresponding entries of `a` and `b`. -/
def intersect {n m : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (b : Vector Float m) : Vector Float (min n m) :=
  Vector.ofFn fun (i : Fin (min n m)) =>
    let x := a[i.val]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le i.isLt (Nat.min_le_left n m))
    let y := b[i.val]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le i.isLt (Nat.min_le_right n m))
    if x ≤ y then x else y

/-- Specification: each entry of the intersection is the minimum
    (with respect to `≤` on floats) of the corresponding entries. -/
theorem intersect_getElem {n m : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (b : Vector Float m)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < min n m) :
    (intersect a b)[i]'h =
      (if a[i]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le h (Nat.min_le_left n m))
            ≤ b[i]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le h (Nat.min_le_right n m))
       then a[i]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le h (Nat.min_le_left n m))
       else b[i]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le h (Nat.min_le_right n m))) := by
  simp [intersect, Vector.getElem_ofFn]

/-- Each entry of the intersection comes from one of the two inputs. -/
theorem intersect_getElem_cases {n m : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (b : Vector Float m)
    (i : Nat) (h : i < min n m) :
    (intersect a b)[i]'h = a[i]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le h (Nat.min_le_left n m)) ∨
    (intersect a b)[i]'h = b[i]'(Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le h (Nat.min_le_right n m)) := by
  rw [intersect_getElem]
  split
  · exact Or.inl rfl
  · exact Or.inr rfl

/-- The length of the intersection is the minimum of the input lengths. -/
theorem intersect_size {n m : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) (b : Vector Float m) :
    (intersect a b).toArray.size = min n m := by
  simp

/-- Bitwise inversion of every element of `a`, viewed as a `bitWidth`-bit
unsigned number: each `x` is first truncated to `bitWidth` bits and then
all of its bits are flipped, i.e. `x ↦ (2^bitWidth - 1) - (x % 2^bitWidth)`. -/
def invert {n : Nat} (bitWidth : Nat) (a : Vector Nat n) : Vector Nat n :=
  a.map (fun x => 2 ^ bitWidth - 1 - x % 2 ^ bitWidth)

/-- Pointwise characterisation. -/
theorem invert_get {n : Nat} (w : Nat) (a : Vector Nat n) (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (invert w a)[i] = 2 ^ w - 1 - a[i] % 2 ^ w := by
  simp [invert]

/-- Every result fits in `w` bits. -/
theorem invert_lt {n : Nat} (w : Nat) (a : Vector Nat n) (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (invert w a)[i] < 2 ^ w := by
  rw [invert_get]
  have hp := Nat.two_pow_pos w
  generalize 2 ^ w = M at *
  generalize a[i] % M = r
  omega

/-- An element and its inversion (truncated to `w` bits) sum to the all-ones
value `2^w - 1`, i.e. they are bitwise complements. -/
theorem invert_add {n : Nat} (w : Nat) (a : Vector Nat n) (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (invert w a)[i] + a[i] % 2 ^ w = 2 ^ w - 1 := by
  rw [invert_get]
  have hp := Nat.two_pow_pos w
  have h2 := Nat.mod_lt a[i] hp
  generalize 2 ^ w = M at *
  generalize a[i] % M = r at *
  omega

/-- Inverting twice gives back the truncated value. -/
theorem invert_invert_get {n : Nat} (w : Nat) (a : Vector Nat n) (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (invert w (invert w a))[i] = a[i] % 2 ^ w := by
  rw [invert_get, invert_get]
  have hp := Nat.two_pow_pos w
  have h2 := Nat.mod_lt a[i] hp
  have h1 : 2 ^ w - 1 - a[i] % 2 ^ w < 2 ^ w := by
    generalize 2 ^ w = M at *
    generalize a[i] % M = r at *
    omega
  rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h1]
  generalize 2 ^ w = M at *
  generalize a[i] % M = r at *
  omega

/-- On vectors whose entries all fit in `w` bits, `invert w` is an involution. -/
theorem invert_invert {n : Nat} (w : Nat) (a : Vector Nat n)
    (h : ∀ i (hi : i < n), a[i] < 2 ^ w) :
    invert w (invert w a) = a := by
  apply Vector.ext
  intro i hi
  rw [invert_invert_get]
  exact Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (h i hi)

    isAlphaStr s = true ↔

  unfold isAlphaStr
  generalize s.toList = l
  cases l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons c cs => simp [List.all_eq_true]

  simp only [isAlpha, Vector.getElem_map]
  exact isAlphaStr_iff input[i]

  Vector.ofFn (fun i : Fin n =>
    decide (-tol ≤ (a[i.1]'i.2) - (b[i.1]'i.2) ∧ (a[i.1]'i.2) - (b[i.1]'i.2) ≤ tol))

  unfold np_isclose
  simp

    (i : Nat) (h : i < n) :
    (np_isclose a b tol)[i] = true ↔ (-tol ≤ a[i] - b[i] ∧ a[i] - b[i] ≤ tol) := by
  rw [np_isclose_getElem]
  simp

  apply decide_eq_decide.mpr

  · intro ⟨h1, h2⟩

def maxUpTo {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (h : n > 0) : Nat → Int
  | 0 => a[0]'h
  | k + 1 =>
    if hk : k + 1 < n then
      (if maxUpTo a h k ≤ a[k+1]'hk then a[k+1]'hk else maxUpTo a h k)
    else maxUpTo a h k

  maxUpTo a h (n - 1)

    ∀ k i (hi : i < n), i ≤ k → a[i]'hi ≤ maxUpTo a h k := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro i hi hik
    have : i = 0 := by omega
    subst this
    simp [maxUpTo]
  | succ k ih =>
    intro i hi hik
    simp only [maxUpTo]
    split
    · rename_i hk
      by_cases hik' : i ≤ k
      · have h1 := ih i hi hik'
        split
        · rename_i h2
          exact Int.le_trans h1 h2
        · exact h1
      · have : i = k + 1 := by omega
        subst this
        split
        · exact Int.le_refl _
        · rename_i h2
          exact Int.le_of_lt (Int.not_le.mp h2)
    · rename_i hk
      exact ih i hi (by omega)

    ∀ k, ∃ i, ∃ hi : i < n, a[i]'hi = maxUpTo a h k := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => exact ⟨0, h, by simp [maxUpTo]⟩
  | succ k ih =>
    obtain ⟨j, hj, e⟩ := ih
    simp only [maxUpTo]
    split
    · rename_i hk
      split
      · exact ⟨k + 1, hk, rfl⟩
      · exact ⟨j, hj, e⟩
    · exact ⟨j, hj, e⟩

    cs[j] v = true →
    (∀ k (hk : k < cs.length), k < j → cs[k] v = false) →
    evalAt v cs fs = fs[j] v
  | [], _, j, hj, _, _, _ => absurd hj (by simp)
  | _ :: _, [], j, _, hf, _, _ => absurd hf (by simp)
  | c :: cs, f :: fs, 0, _, _, hc, _ => by
      have hc' : c v = true := hc
      simp [evalAt, hc']
  | c :: cs, f :: fs, j+1, hj, hf, hc, h => by
      have h0 : c v = false := h 0 (by simp) (by omega)
      have hj' : j < cs.length := by simp at hj; omega
      have hf' : j < fs.length := by simp at hf; omega

          have := h (k+1) (by simp; omega) (by omega)
          exact this)
      simp only [evalAt, h0, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, ite_false]
      exact ih

/-- `poly_helper roots val` returns the coefficients, highest degree first, of
    `∏_{j < min val n} (x - roots[j])`.
    Only the first `n` coefficients are kept: index `i` holds the coefficient of
    `x^(deg - i)`. The leading coefficient (index 0) is always `1`.
    Each step multiplies the current coefficient vector `c` by `(x - r)`:
    `new[0] = c[0]` and `new[i] = c[i] - r * c[i-1]` for `i > 0`. -/
def poly_helper {n : Nat} (roots : Vector Float n) (val : Nat) : Vector Float n :=
  match val with
  | 0 => Vector.ofFn fun i => if i.val = 0 then 1.0 else 0.0
  | k+1 =>
    let c := poly_helper roots k
    if h : k < n then
      Vector.ofFn fun i =>
        if i.val = 0 then c[i]
        else c[i] - roots[k] * c[i.val - 1]'(by have := i.isLt; omega)
    else c

/-- Coefficients (highest degree first, truncated to length `n`) of the monic
    polynomial whose roots are `roots`. -/
def poly {n : Nat} (roots : Vector Float n) : Vector Float n :=
  poly_helper roots n

    (poly_helper roots 0)[i] = (if i = 0 then 1.0 else 0.0) := by
  simp [poly_helper]

    ∀ val, (poly_helper roots val)[0]'h = 1.0
  | 0 => by simp [poly_helper]
  | k+1 => by
    have ih := poly_helper_head roots h k
    simp only [poly_helper]
    split
    · simp [ih]
    · exact ih

  simp [poly_helper, hk]

  have : i ≠ 0 := by omega
  simp [poly_helper, hk, this]

def derivOnce {n : Nat} (p : Vector Float n) : Vector Float (n - 1) :=
  Vector.ofFn fun (i : Fin (n - 1)) =>
    p[i.val]'(by have := i.isLt; omega) * (n - 1 - i.val).toFloat

/-- Iterate the derivative `k` times. -/
def derivIter : (k : Nat) → {n : Nat} → Vector Float n → Vector Float (n - k)
  | 0, _, p => p.cast (by omega)
  | k + 1, _, p => (derivIter k (derivOnce p)).cast (by omega)

  derivIter m.natAbs poly

    (derivOnce p)[i] = p[i]'(by omega) * (n - 1 - i).toFloat := by
  first

  | simp [derivOnce]

  | zero => simp [prodArray]
  | succ k =>

      prodArray a start k * (if hk : k < n then a[k] else 1) := by
  simp only [prodArray, if_pos h]

  rw [prodArray_succ a (Nat.le_refl k), prodArray_empty a (Nat.le_refl k), dif_pos h]

    have hs : start = 0 := by omega

    simp [prodArray]

      simp
    · rw [prodArray_succ a (by omega : start ≤ k), prodArray_succ a (by omega : mid ≤ k),

  | _, 0 => 0.0
  | j, fuel + 1 => if c j then x j else pickFrom c x (j + 1) fuel

where `k` is the first index with `condlist[k][i] = true`, or `0.0` if no
condition holds at `i`. -/

  Vector.ofFn fun (i : Fin n) =>
    pickFrom
      (fun j => if h : j < m then (condlist[j]'h)[i.1]'i.2 else false)
      (fun j => if h : j < m then (choicelist[j]'h)[i.1]'i.2 else 0.0)
      0 m

      pickFrom c x j fuel = x k := by

  induction fuel with
  | zero => intro j k h1 h2; omega
  | succ f ih =>
    intro j k h1 h2 h3 h4
    simp only [pickFrom]
    by_cases hjk : j = k
    · subst hjk
      rw [if_pos h4]
    · have hj : c j = false := h3 j (Nat.le_refl _) (by omega)
      rw [if_neg (by simp [hj])]
      exact ih (j+1) k (by omega) (by omega) (fun l hl1 hl2 => h3 l (by omega) hl2) h4

  | succ f ih =>

/-!
Sorting a `Vector Float n`.

`Float` comparison (`<`, `≤`) is opaque in core Lean and is not a total order
because of NaN, so sortedness with respect to it cannot be proved. Instead we
sort by an IEEE-754 total-order key computed from the bit pattern:

* negative floats (sign bit set) are mapped to `2^64 - 1 - bits`;
* non-negative floats are mapped to `bits + 2^63`.

For non-NaN values this key is monotone in the numeric order, with `-0 < +0`.
That connection to the numeric order is not proved here.
-/

def floatKey (x : Float) : Nat :=
  let b := x.toBits.toNat
  if b ≥ 2 ^ 63 then 2 ^ 64 - 1 - b else b + 2 ^ 63

def insertK (x : Float) : List Float → List Float
  | [] => [x]
  | y :: ys => if floatKey x ≤ floatKey y then x :: y :: ys else y :: insertK x ys

def isortK : List Float → List Float
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => insertK x (isortK xs)

theorem insertK_length (x : Float) (l : List Float) :
    (insertK x l).length = l.length + 1 := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons y ys ih =>
    unfold insertK
    split
    · rfl
    · simp [ih]

theorem isortK_length (l : List Float) : (isortK l).length = l.length := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih => simp [isortK, insertK_length, ih]

def sort {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) : Vector Float n :=
  ⟨(isortK a.toList).toArray, by simp [isortK_length]⟩

theorem sort_toList {n : Nat} (a : Vector Float n) :
    (sort a).toList = isortK a.toList := rfl

theorem insertK_perm (x : Float) (l : List Float) :
    (insertK x l).Perm (x :: l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => exact List.Perm.refl _
  | cons y ys ih =>
    unfold insertK
    split
    · exact List.Perm.refl _
    · exact (List.Perm.cons y ih).trans (List.Perm.swap x y ys)

theorem isortK_perm (l : List Float) : (isortK l).Perm l := by
  induction l with
  | nil => exact List.Perm.refl _
  | cons x xs ih => exact (insertK_perm x _).trans (ih.cons x)

theorem insertK_pairwise (x : Float) (l : List Float)
    (h : l.Pairwise (fun a b => floatKey a ≤ floatKey b)) :
    (insertK x l).Pairwise (fun a b => floatKey a ≤ floatKey b) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [insertK]
  | cons y ys ih =>
    have h' := List.pairwise_cons.1 h
    unfold insertK
    split
    · rename_i hxy
      rw [List.pairwise_cons]
      refine ⟨?_, h⟩
      intro z hz
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hz with rfl | hz
      · exact hxy
      · have := h'.1 z hz
        omega
    · rename_i hxy
      rw [List.pairwise_cons]
      refine ⟨?_, ih h'.2⟩
      intro z hz
      have hm := (insertK_perm x ys).mem_iff.1 hz
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hm with rfl | hz'
      · omega
      · exact h'.1 z hz'

    (isortK l).Pairwise (fun a b => floatKey a ≤ floatKey b) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => exact List.Pairwise.nil
  | cons x xs ih => exact insertK_pairwise x _ ih

  rw [sort_toList]
  exact isortK_perm _

    (sort a).toList.Pairwise (fun x y => floatKey x ≤ floatKey y) := by
  rw [sort_toList]
  exact isortK_sorted _

/-- Sum of the elements of `a` with indices in the half-open range `[start, finish)`.
Indices that are `≥ n` contribute `0`. -/
def sumArray {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (start finish : Nat) : Int :=
  match finish with
  | 0 => 0
  | k + 1 =>
    if start ≤ k then
      sumArray a start k + (if h : k < n then a[k] else 0)
    else 0

/-- Sum of all the elements of `a`. -/
def sum {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) : Int :=
  sumArray a 0 n

/-! ## Specification -/

/-- `sum` is the range sum over the whole vector. -/
theorem sum_eq_sumArray {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) : sum a = sumArray a 0 n := rfl

/-- The sum of an empty vector is zero. -/
theorem sum_zero (a : Vector Int 0) : sum a = 0 := rfl

/-- An empty (or reversed) range sums to zero. -/
theorem sumArray_empty {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (s f : Nat) (h : f ≤ s) :
    sumArray a s f = 0 := by
  cases f with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k =>
    have hk : ¬ s ≤ k := by omega
    simp [sumArray, hk]

/-- Extending the range by one element on the right adds that element. -/
theorem sumArray_succ {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (s k : Nat) (h : s ≤ k) :
    sumArray a s (k + 1) = sumArray a s k + (if h : k < n then a[k] else 0) := by
  simp [sumArray, h]

/-- Extending the range by an in-bounds element adds exactly `a[k]`. -/
theorem sumArray_succ_of_lt {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (s k : Nat) (h : s ≤ k)
    (hk : k < n) :
    sumArray a s (k + 1) = sumArray a s k + a[k] := by
  rw [sumArray_succ a s k h]
  simp [hk]

/-- A single-element range sums to that element. -/
theorem sumArray_single {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (i : Nat) (hi : i < n) :
    sumArray a i (i + 1) = a[i] := by
  rw [sumArray_succ_of_lt a i i (Nat.le_refl _) hi,
      sumArray_empty a i i (Nat.le_refl _)]
  simp

/-- Range sums are additive over adjacent ranges. -/
theorem sumArray_split {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (s m f : Nat)
    (hs : s ≤ m) (hmf : m ≤ f) :
    sumArray a s m + sumArray a m f = sumArray a s f := by
  induction f with
  | zero =>
    have h1 : m = 0 := by omega
    have h2 : s = 0 := by omega
    subst h1
    subst h2
    rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    by_cases hmk : m ≤ k
    · rw [sumArray_succ a s k (by omega), sumArray_succ a m k hmk, ← ih hmk]
      exact (Int.add_assoc _ _ _).symm
    · have hm : m = k + 1 := by omega
      subst hm
      rw [sumArray_empty a (k + 1) (k + 1) (Nat.le_refl _)]
      simp

    tril arr k i j = (if ((j.val : Int) - (i.val : Int) ≤ k) then arr i j else 0) := rfl

theorem tril_apply_le {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (k : Int) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n)
    (h : (j.val : Int) - (i.val : Int) ≤ k) : tril arr k i j = arr i j := by
  simp only [tril]
  simp [h]

theorem tril_apply_gt {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (k : Int) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n)
    (h : k < (j.val : Int) - (i.val : Int)) : tril arr k i j = 0 := by
  have h' : ¬ ((j.val : Int) - (i.val : Int) ≤ k) := Int.not_le.mpr h
  simp only [tril]
  simp [h']

/-- Deduplicate a list, keeping the first occurrence of each element (in order). -/
def dedup : List Int → List Int
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => x :: (dedup xs).filter (fun y => y != x)

/-- Pad a list up to length `n` by repeating its first element. -/
def padList (n : Nat) (l : List Int) : List Int :=
  l ++ List.replicate (n - l.length) (l.headD 0)

theorem mem_dedup (y : Int) : ∀ l : List Int, y ∈ dedup l ↔ y ∈ l
  | [] => by simp [dedup]
  | x :: xs => by
    simp only [dedup, List.mem_cons, List.mem_filter, mem_dedup y xs]
    by_cases h : y = x <;> simp [h]

theorem length_dedup : ∀ l : List Int, (dedup l).length ≤ l.length
  | [] => by simp [dedup]
  | x :: xs => by
    simp only [dedup, List.length_cons]
    have h1 := List.length_filter_le (fun y => y != x) (dedup xs)
    have h2 := length_dedup xs
    omega

theorem nodup_dedup : ∀ l : List Int, (dedup l).Nodup
  | [] => List.nodup_nil
  | x :: xs => by
    simp only [dedup]
    apply List.nodup_cons.mpr
    constructor
    · simp [List.mem_filter]
    · exact List.Pairwise.sublist (List.filter_sublist ..) (nodup_dedup xs)

/-- Returns the unique values of `arr` (in order of first occurrence),
    padded to length `n` by repeating the first unique value. -/
def unique_all {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) : Vector Int n :=
  ⟨(padList n (dedup arr.toArray.toList)).toArray, by
    have h1 := length_dedup arr.toArray.toList
    have h2 : arr.toArray.toList.length = n := by simp
    show (padList n (dedup arr.toArray.toList)).length = n
    simp only [padList, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]
    omega⟩

theorem mem_pad (n : Nat) (L : List Int) (hL : L.length = n) (x : Int) :
    x ∈ padList n (dedup L) ↔ x ∈ L := by
  cases L with
  | nil =>
    subst hL
    simp [padList, dedup]
  | cons a t =>
    unfold padList
    rw [List.mem_append, List.mem_replicate]
    constructor
    · rintro (h | ⟨_, rfl⟩)
      · exact (mem_dedup _ _).1 h
      · simp [dedup]
    · intro h
      exact Or.inl ((mem_dedup _ _).2 h)

/-- The result list is exactly the padded deduplication. -/
theorem unique_all_toList {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) :
    (unique_all arr).toArray.toList = padList n (dedup arr.toArray.toList) := rfl

/-- Every value in the result occurs in the input, and vice versa. -/
theorem unique_all_mem {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) (x : Int) :
    x ∈ (unique_all arr).toArray.toList ↔ x ∈ arr.toArray.toList := by
  rw [unique_all_toList]
  exact mem_pad n _ (by simp) x

/-- The result begins with the distinct values of the input (first-occurrence order). -/
theorem unique_all_prefix {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) :
    dedup arr.toArray.toList <+: (unique_all arr).toArray.toList := ⟨_, rfl⟩

/-- That prefix contains no duplicates. -/
theorem unique_all_prefix_nodup {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) :
    (dedup arr.toArray.toList).Nodup := nodup_dedup _

/-- That prefix contains every value of the input. -/
theorem unique_all_prefix_complete {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) (x : Int) :
    x ∈ arr.toArray.toList → x ∈ dedup arr.toArray.toList :=
  (mem_dedup x _).2
